{{Short description|Danish mathematician (1867–1944)}}
[[File:Carl_Burrau.jpg|thumb]]
'''Carl Jensen Burrau''' (29 July 1867 – 8 October 1944) was a Danish mathematician who worked on problems relating to physics and astronomy while also working as an actuary.

Burrau was born in [[Helsingør|Helsingör]] (Elsinore), Denmark and was educated at [[University of Copenhagen|Copenhagen University]]. He worked as an astronomy assistant at the university observatory from 1893 to 1898. He is known for his work on a three-body problem, examining the orbits of two equal masses revolving about each other.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Valtonen|first1=M. J.|last2=Mikkola|first2=S.|last3=Pietilä|first3=H.|date=1995|title=Burrau's three-body problem in the post-Newtonian approximation|journal=Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society|language=en|volume=273|issue=3|pages=751–754|doi=10.1093/mnras/273.3.751|issn=0035-8711|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Szebehely|first=Victor|date=1967|title=Burrau's Problem of Three Bodies|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America|volume=58|issue=1|pages=60–65|doi=10.1073/pnas.58.1.60|jstor=58171|pmid=16578651|pmc=335596|bibcode=1967PNAS...58...60S|issn=0027-8424|doi-access=free}}</ref> His collaborations with [[Thorvald N. Thiele|Törvald Thiele]] led to the so-called Thiele–Burrau method. His dissertation of 1895 examines methods of identifying constants from photographs of star positions using Bessel's classic method.<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Valtonen, M. J.|author2=  Mikkola, S.|author3= Pietilä, H.| year=1995| title= Burrau's Three-Body Problem in the Post-Newtonian Approximation| journal= Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society|volume= 273|issue= 3|page= 751|doi= 10.1093/mnras/273.3.751|doi-access= free}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Burrau, Carl|year=1913|title=Numerische Berechnung eines Spezialfalles des Dreikorperproblems|url=http://adsabs.harvard.edu/pdf/1913AN....195..113B|journal=Astronomische Nachrichten|volume=195|issue=4662|pages=6–8|doi=10.1002/asna.19131950602|bibcode=1913AN....195..113B}}</ref> He then worked on actuarial mathematics, writing a book on the subject, ''Forsikringsstatistikens Grundlag'' (1925), and taught applied mathematics at Copenhagen university.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Kristensen, S.|title= Carl Burrau| journal= Scandinavian Actuarial Journal |year=1945|volume= 1945|issue=1–2|pages= 128–130| doi=10.1080/03461238.1945.10404922 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Burrau|first=Carl|date=1934|title=The half-invariants of the sum of two typical laws of errors, with an application to the problem of dissecting a frequency curve into components|url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/03461238.1934.10419229|journal=Scandinavian Actuarial Journal|language=en|volume=1934|issue=1|pages=1–6|doi=10.1080/03461238.1934.10419229|bibcode=1934PCopO..93....1B|issn=0346-1238|url-access=subscription}}</ref>
